title: Fixed-size subset sums: sharp support, Rényi entropy and tail bounds
shortTitle: Random subset sums: how concentrated can they be?
oneLine: If n numbers add to zero, at least 2·C(n−2, k−1) of the k-subsets have a nonzero sum, and only (1, −1, 0, …, 0) attains it, proving a 2018 conjecture on Johnson graphs; the paper also finds the exact minimum Rényi entropy of a random subset sum and proves the hypergeometric tail bound from n = 4k.
abstract: Choose k of n given real numbers uniformly at random, without replacement, and add them. How concentrated can such a fixed-size subset sum be? This candidate answers three classical forms of the question exactly. Zero sums: if the numbers add up to zero and are not all zero, at least 2·C(n−2, k−1) of the k-subsets have a nonzero sum whenever k ≥ 5 and n ≥ 2k + 1, with equality only for (1, −1, 0, …, 0) up to scaling and reordering. This is the smallest support of an eigenfunction in the first nontrivial eigenspace of the Johnson graph, and proves the 2018 conjecture of Mogilnykh, Vorob’ev and Valyuzhenich, who had checked it by computer for n ≤ 600; a formula with all equality cases is given for every n and k, including one small case, (1, 1, −1, −1, 0) at n = 5, k = 2, that earlier classifications missed. Entropy: the minimum Rényi entropy of the sum is found for every order, answering a question of Ai, Kuželka and Pelekis (2026). One outlier is optimal except at half-sampling (n = 2k), where two outliers win above an explicit order α_k (α_2 = 2, about 1.386k for large k), so the universal Bernoulli lower bound holds exactly for orders up to 2. Tails: for two-valued populations the probability that the sum is at least its mean is at least k/n whenever n ≥ 4k, extending the range n ≥ 8k of Ai and Pelekis (2026) with a 2026 lemma of Ai, Karagiannis, Kuželka and Pelekis; so the Aydinian–Blinovsky conjecture would imply the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture for all n ≥ 4k. This does not prove that conjecture. Exact analogues over Abelian groups and a small-ball inequality are included. Limits: real numbers only for the zero-sum theorem, first Johnson eigenspace only, tail problem below 4k open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

evidence: A 19-page paper with a plain introduction (the question, what was known, notation, main results, what is new and what is not, roadmap) and complete written proofs of every result; no step of a proof is computational. Five standard-library Python scripts check the statements exactly on finite ranges, each in seconds: the support formula and minimisers on all zero-sum vectors with entries in {−2, …, 2} for n ≤ 10 and a complete certificate for n ≤ 7; hypergeometric atoms, the parity majorization chain and the entropy equality statements; the integer-mean lemma for n ≤ 300; the tail theorem for k ≤ 40 and 4k ≤ n ≤ 10k (930,660 cases); and the counterexamples over Z_2, Z_3 and Z_5. Clean replay from fresh copies in normal and python -O mode reproduced every output, and a weakened check makes the scripts fail.

keyResults: Theorem 1.1 (proof): for a nonzero zero-sum vector, at least 2·C(n−2, k−1) of the k-subsets have a nonzero sum when k ≥ 5 and n ≥ 2k + 1, with equality only for (1, −1, 0, …, 0) up to scaling and reordering (Conjecture 1 of Mogilnykh, Vorob’ev and Valyuzhenich, 2018); the complete formula and all minimisers for every n and k, including (1, 1, −1, −1, 0) at (n, k) = (5, 2).

Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 (proofs): the law of a random k-subset sum is majorized by Ber(k/n) away from half-sampling and by U or Q_k at n = 2k; hence the exact minimum Rényi entropy for every order, with the crossover order α_k at half-sampling (α_2 = 2, α_k ≈ (2k − ½) ln 2).
Corollary 1.4 (proof): the universal Bernoulli bound H_α(X) ≥ H_α(Ber(k/n)) holds for all populations if and only if 0 < α ≤ 2.

Theorem 1.5 (proof): P(Hyp(n, i, k) ≥ ik/n) ≥ k/n for n ≥ 4k, with a single outlier the unique minimiser for n > 4k; Corollary 7.2: the Aydinian–Blinovsky conjecture would imply the Manickam–Miklós–Singhi conjecture for n ≥ 4k.
Theorem 1.6 (proof): the exact minimum support of degree-one functions on Boolean slices over every nontrivial Abelian group, and an entropy dichotomy decided by elements of order two.

narration: Fixed-size subset sums: an Evidence Press briefing. Pick some numbers from a list at random and add them up. How predictable can that sum be? This candidate answers exactly, in three senses. First, how often can the sum be zero? If the numbers add up to zero and are not all zero, and you pick k of the n numbers, the paper proves that at least two times n minus two choose k minus one of the picks give a nonzero sum, whenever k is at least five and n is larger than twice k. Only one pattern achieves this: a single plus one, a single minus one, and zeros everywhere else. In graph theory, this is the smallest footprint of a vibration mode of the Johnson graph. Mogilnykh, Vorob'ev and Valyuzhenich conjectured it in twenty eighteen, after checking every n up to six hundred by computer. Second, how predictable can the whole distribution be, measured by Rényi entropy? A single outlier gives the most predictable sum, except when exactly half the numbers are drawn: then two outliers win, once the order of the entropy passes an explicit threshold. So a natural Bernoulli lower bound holds for every population exactly when the order is at most two, and fails beyond it. Third, how rarely can the sum be nonnegative? Aydinian and Blinovsky conjectured that lists with just two distinct values are the worst case for the Manickam, Miklós and Singhi conjecture, which asks how many picks from a zero-sum list must have a nonnegative sum. For those lists the paper proves the expected bound whenever n is at least four times k, where earlier work needed eight times k, using a recent lemma of Ai, Karagiannis, Kuželka and Pelekis. So their conjecture would imply the full Manickam, Miklós and Singhi conjecture; this does not prove it. The limits matter: the zero-sum theorem is for real numbers, only the first eigenspace is treated, and the computer checks supplement the written proofs. Evidence Press published this anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, and its review was internal, not peer review. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

decisionObject.description: Treat the minimum support of the first Johnson eigenspace as 2·C(n−2, k−1) for k ≥ 5, n ≥ 2k + 1 (MVV Conjecture 1), the minimum Rényi entropy of fixed-size subset sums as given by one or two outliers with crossover α_k, and the two-valued hypergeometric tail bound k/n as valid from n = 4k.
decisionObject.scope: Real populations and the first Johnson eigenspace; the MMS consequence is conditional on the Aydinian–Blinovsky conjecture; the tail problem below 4k remains open.
